title: Amygdalin attenuates post-ischemic neuroinflammation by targeting TLR4/NF-kappaB signaling and NLRP3 inflammasome in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
authors: Wang, Yan-Chen; Wang, Hong-Yan; Yuan, Yi-Fan; Zhang, Zi-Jian; Wang, Yi-Han; Liu, Jing-Jie; Peng, Liang; Zhang, Gang; Gao, Jing; Yan, Yong-Gang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究苦杏仁苷通过TLR4/NF-kB/NLRP3通路减轻脑缺血再灌注损伤的神经炎症，属于纯湿实验与药理学研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is a major contributor to neuronal damage after ischemic stroke, and current therapies remain limited by a narrow therapeutic window and reperfusion-associated injury. Amygdalin (Amg) has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, but its role in regulating microglial polarization, pyroptosis, and the TLR4/NF-kappaB/NLRP3 axis in CIRI remains unclear. In this study, rat MCAO/R and BV-2 cell OGD/R models were used to evaluate the protective effects of Amg in vivo and in vitro. Transcriptomics, untargeted metabolomics, integrated pathway analysis, and molecular docking were combined with qPCR, Western blotting, LPS/ATP stimulation, and inhibitor interventions using TAK-242 and MCC950. Amg enhanced BV-2 cell viability, reduced OGD/R-induced pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and restored antioxidant enzyme activities. In MCAO/R rats, Amg significantly improved neurological function and alleviated brain tissue damage. In addition, Amg attenuated inflammation and oxidative stress, suppressed microglial M1 polarization while promoting M2-related phenotypes, and reduced pyroptosis-related marker expression in vivo and in vitro. Integrated multi-omics analysis further narrowed the candidate mechanisms to core pathways including NF-kappaB, Toll-like receptor, and NOD-like receptor signaling, and identified Tlr4, Myd88, Nlrp3, and Caspase-1 as key candidate molecules; pharmacological dissection experiments showed that combined treatment with Amg and either a TLR4 inhibitor or an NLRP3 inhibitor did not produce a significant additional synergistic effect, suggesting that its protective action depends on regulation of the TLR4/NF-kappaB/NLRP3-signaling axis. These findings provide mechanistic evidence for the neuroprotective effects of Amg in CIRI and support its potential as a therapeutic candidate for ischemic stroke.
abstract_zh: 脑缺血再灌注损伤（CIRI）是缺血性卒中后神经元损伤的主要因素，而当前治疗仍受限于狭窄的治疗时间窗和再灌注相关损伤。苦杏仁苷（Amg）具有抗炎和抗氧化活性，但其在CIRI中调节小胶质细胞极化、焦亡及TLR4/NF-kappaB/NLRP3轴的作用尚不清楚。本研究采用大鼠MCAO/R和BV-2细胞OGD/R模型，评估Amg在体内和体外的保护作用。转录组学、非靶向代谢组学、整合通路分析及分子对接，结合qPCR、Western blotting、LPS/ATP刺激及TAK-242和MCC950抑制剂干预进行综合研究。Amg增强了BV-2细胞活力，减少了OGD/R诱导的促炎细胞因子释放，并恢复了抗氧化酶活性。在MCAO/R大鼠中，Amg显著改善了神经功能并减轻了脑组织损伤。此外，Amg在体内和体外减弱了炎症和氧化应激，抑制了小胶质细胞M1极化同时促进M2相关表型，并降低了焦亡相关标志物的表达。整合多组学分析进一步将候选机制缩小至核心通路，包括NF-kappaB、Toll样受体和NOD样受体信号通路，并鉴定Tlr4、Myd88、Nlrp3和Caspase-1为关键候选分子；药理学解析实验显示，Amg与TLR4抑制剂或NLRP3抑制剂联合治疗未产生显著的额外协同效应，表明其保护作用依赖于对TLR4/NF-kappaB/NLRP3信号轴的调控。这些发现为Amg在CIRI中的神经保护作用提供了机制证据，并支持其作为缺血性卒中治疗候选药物的潜力。
